groups.title: Programming languages
groups.intro: The languages you are most likely to read or write on client work, each with a path from first steps to the official reference.

items.name: Python
items.why: Python is the main language for data work, scripts and AI. Most LLM SDKs, agent frameworks and data tools are Python first, so it is the language you will use most on client work.

links.title: Learn Python - Full Course for Beginners [Tutorial]
CS50's Introduction to Programming with Python
Transforming Code into Beautiful, Idiomatic Python
James Powell: So you want to be a Python expert? | PyData Seattle 2017

items.name: JavaScript
items.why: JavaScript runs every web page and, with Node.js, many servers. You need it to build the screens and small web apps that let a client use an AI feature.

links.title: Learn JavaScript - Full Course for Beginners
What the heck is the event loop anyway? | Philip Roberts | JSConf EU
Jake Archibald on the web browser event loop, setTimeout, micro tasks, requestAnimationFrame, ...

items.name: TypeScript
items.why: TypeScript is JavaScript with types. Most modern web apps and many AI SDKs use it, and the types catch mistakes before the code runs.

links.title: TypeScript Course for Beginners - Learn TypeScript from Scratch!

items.name: Go
items.why: Go is a simple, fast language for backend services, command line tools and cloud software. Docker, Kubernetes and Terraform are written in Go, and it is a good fit for the services that sit around an AI model.

links.title: Learn Go Programming - Golang Tutorial for Beginners
Golang Tutorial for Beginners | Full Go Course

items.name: Rust
items.why: Rust is a fast systems language that prevents whole classes of memory bugs. It shows up in performance critical parts of AI tooling, such as tokenizers and inference servers.

links.title: The Rust Programming Language (The Rust Book)

items.name: Java
items.why: Java runs a large share of enterprise backends, banking and ERP integrations. On client work you will often read or call Java services when you connect AI to existing systems.

links.title: Learn Java 8 - Full Tutorial for Beginners

items.name: C#
items.why: C# is Microsoft's main language for .NET backends, desktop apps and Azure services. Many enterprise clients run on it, so you will meet it when you integrate AI into Microsoft based systems.

links.title: C# Tutorial - Full Course for Beginners
Write your first code using C# (Get started with C#, Part 1)
C# Tutorial For Beginners - Learn C# Basics in 1 Hour

items.name: SQL
items.why: SQL is how you ask questions of a database. Almost every client keeps its business data in SQL databases, and you will query it to feed, check and measure AI features.

links.title: SQL Tutorial - Full Database Course for Beginners
CS50's Introduction to Databases with SQL
#01 - Relational Model & Algebra (CMU Intro to Database Systems)

items.name: Bash and the shell
items.why: The shell is the text interface to a computer. You use it to run scripts, move files, check logs and drive tools like Git, Docker and cloud command line tools on servers.

groups.title: DevOps and delivery
groups.intro: The tools that take code from your laptop to a running, monitored system at the client.

items.name: Linux command line
items.why: Most servers, containers and cloud machines run Linux. You need to move around, read logs and fix things on a Linux box without a graphical screen.

links.title: The 50 Most Popular Linux & Terminal Commands - Full Course for Beginners
The Linux command line for beginners
100+ Linux Things you Need to Know
The Missing Semester of Your CS Education

items.name: Git and GitHub
items.why: Git tracks every change to code and GitHub is where teams share it, review it and run automation. Every client project you touch will live in a Git repository.

links.title: Git and GitHub for Beginners - Crash Course
Git Tutorial for Beginners: Learn Git in 1 Hour
Git for Professionals Tutorial - Tools & Concepts for Mastering Version Control with Git

items.name: Docker
items.why: Docker packages an app with everything it needs into a container, so it runs the same on a laptop and on a server. It is the usual way to ship an AI service to a client.

links.title: Docker Crash Course for Absolute Beginners [NEW]
Docker Tutorial for Beginners [FULL COURSE in 3 Hours]
Build and share a containerized application
Complete Docker Course - From BEGINNER to PRO! (Learn Containers)

items.name: Kubernetes
items.why: Kubernetes runs many containers across many machines and restarts them when they fail. Larger clients run their services on it, so you need to deploy to it and read what it is doing.

links.title: Kubernetes Crash Course for Absolute Beginners [NEW]
Kubernetes Tutorial for Beginners [FULL COURSE in 4 Hours]
Kubernetes Course - Full Beginners Tutorial (Containerize Your Apps!)
Kubernetes Explained in 6 Minutes | k8s Architecture

items.name: CI/CD with GitHub Actions
items.why: CI/CD runs your tests and deploys your code automatically on every change. GitHub Actions is the most common way to set this up for a project hosted on GitHub.

links.title: 5 Ways to DevOps-ify your App - Github Actions Tutorial
GitHub Actions Tutorial - Basic Concepts and CI/CD Pipeline with Docker
Github Actions CI/CD - Everything you need to know to get started

items.name: Terraform (infrastructure as code)
items.why: Terraform describes cloud resources as code files, so you can create, review and repeat an environment instead of clicking in a console. Many clients use it to control what gets deployed.

links.title: Terraform explained in 15 mins | Terraform Tutorial for Beginners
Get started with Terraform on AWS
Terraform Course - Automate your AWS cloud infrastructure

items.name: Cloud fundamentals
items.why: AWS, Azure and Google Cloud rent out computers, storage, databases and AI models. Every client uses at least one of them, so you need the shared basics: accounts, regions, networks, identity and cost.

links.title: Cloud Computing In 6 Minutes | What Is Cloud Computing? | Cloud Computing Explained | Simplilearn

items.name: Observability (logs, metrics, traces)
items.why: Observability means you can tell what a running system is doing from its logs, metrics and traces. For AI features this is how you see slow calls, errors and cost after go-live.

links.title: How Prometheus Monitoring works | Prometheus Architecture explained
Get started with Grafana Open Source
